# Text-outline miter limits

Original OOXML controls generated by `tools/text_outline_miter_fixture.py` from
our original outline-control package. No corpus artwork or font binaries are
included. The reference application opened the exact source and exported
`native.pdf`. `tools/text_outline_miter_reference.py` verifies the PDF paths,
renders the 96-DPI reference and records source/reference hashes.

Eight rows cover declared limits 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8, an omitted limit, and
explicit bevel joins. MS-DOCX CT_LineJoinMiterProperties defines the limit as a
positive percentage with default zero; ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.1.8.43 describes
the miter join. See the [Open XML SDK definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.office2010.word.linejoinmiterproperties?view=openxml-2.7.1)
and [MS-OI29500 implementation note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/7bd817fb-79cf-4789-b733-4a29f032f5b7).

**Measured native reference compatibility divergence:** all seven miter rows emit miter
joins with PDF's default limit 10, without an explicit M operator or ExtGState
ML. Their normalized paths agree within 0.01pt PDF coordinate rounding. The
bevel row explicitly emits bevel joins. Painting follows that measured behavior;
the original authored limit remains in the model and exported XML. This rule is
specific to text outlines, not shape outlines. Percentage-string lexical forms
and outline color transforms remain unsupported.

The browser compares each native purple outline mask bidirectionally, requiring
99% agreement within one pixel. It checks exact no-edit export, body insertion,
unrelated package parts, exact undo and editable reopen. After editing, native
mask comparison excludes only the intentionally changed first row. Unit tests
check zero/fractional/default import and authored-limit preservation.
